angles: Shift the selection stage from 'which ideas are best' to 'which set of 3 is best': treat the final top 3 as a portfolio and pick it by marginal contribution (a set-level objective over Bradley-Terry / Plackett-Luce strengths plus a measured distance between ideas, e.g. embedding or mechanism-tag distance), so the three cards differ in kind and cover different risk profiles. A single agent picking its own top 3 tends to choose three variants of its favourite idea; a swarm with independent generators has the diversity to fill a portfolio.

Make the multi-agent system's edge come from information the single agent cannot cheaply obtain: use the sandbox and the cross-run idea library as evidence sources. Critics must attach an executable check (a quick simulation, a back-of-envelope calculation, a prior-art or duplicate lookup against the library of past ideas and outcomes) to each objection, and an idea's survival is scored on checks that passed, not on argument quality. This targets critique and development, and it gives an outcome-based measure, the rate of falsified claims in the top 3, that does not depend on rater taste.

domains.text: Evolutionary biology and quality-diversity search (MAP-Elites, novelty search, niche speciation): an archive keeps the best individual in each behavioural niche instead of a single global optimum, and fitness sharing penalises crowding. Transfer: the idea library becomes a niche archive, and the finals draw one champion per niche.

Clinical trial design and adaptive randomisation (multi-armed bandits, group-sequential stopping for futility, blinded independent adjudication of endpoints): allocate more patients to winning arms and stop losing arms early. Transfer: allocate pairwise comparisons and development tokens adaptively by successive halving on Plackett-Luce posteriors, and use a separate adjudicator role that never saw the development stage.
